papers.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a formidable pathogen and the leading cause of skin and soft tissue infections. We recently showed that the highly conserved sasF gene, encoding for an uncharacterized sortase-anchored surface protein, is up-regulated when S. aureus colonizes skin. Here, we demonstrate that SasF is an enzyme that has glycoside epimerase activity, which is required for S. aureus resistance to skin fatty acids. Mutants of sasF are highly impaired in skin colonization and acute infection models. The SasF enzyme is crucial for maintaining the structure of wall teichoic acids and proper S. aureus surface chemistry. To our knowledge, this is the first report of a bacterial surface epimerase in this pathogen, suggesting that SasF could be a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μp = 10.42 cm2 V-1 s-1, μn = 30.23 cm2 V-1 s-1). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml-1 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

papers.abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

papers.abstract: The duration of isolated attosecond pulses created via high-order harmonic generation is determined by the number of optical cycles in the driving laser. Achieving shorter attosecond soft x-ray pulses requires minimizing the number of cycles while maintaining a high pulse energy. Here, we demonstrate a carrier-envelope-phase-stable, 100-mJ-class sub-cycle mid-infrared laser that produces a supercontinuum coherent soft-x-ray with unprecedented bandwidth. The system delivers 50-mJ, 6.7-fs (0.88-cycle) pulses at a center wavelength of 2.26 μm-over two orders of magnitude more energetic than any previous sub-cycle laser. We applied the system to high-order harmonic generation and compared the results to simulations based on the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation to identify unique features of sub-cycle lasers. This work represents a decisive step toward high-energy half-cycle lasers and high-energy single-digit attosecond soft x-ray pulses that can be used to probe matter and light-matter interactions at previously inaccessible temporal resolutions.

papers.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax (P. vivax) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

papers.abstract: Background: Only 3%–5% of patients with cancer nationwide enroll in clinical trials. Although participation among patients with solid tumors has been well studied, data in the hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) setting remain limited. We sought to (1) describe clinical trial participation rates by HSCT type; (2) examine associations between patient, disease, and transplant characteristics and trial participation; and (3) explore the association between trial participation and overall survival (OS). Methods: We conducted a retrospective study using Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) data from US adults aged 18–75 years who underwent autologous or allogeneic HSCT between 2013 and 2019 (N=84,151; autologous: n=51,133; allogeneic: n=33,018). Logistic regression models assessed predictors of participation, while Cox models evaluated associations with OS. Results: Trial participation was 2.0% among patients undergoing autologous HSCT and 11.1% among those undergoing allogeneic HSCT. Among autologous recipients, greater comorbidity burden was associated with lower odds of participation. Patients with multiple myeloma had higher odds than those with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (odds ratio [OR], 1.25; P =.01). Among allogeneic recipients, older adults had higher odds of participation (eg, OR, 2.19 for age ≥70 vs 18–19 years; P <.0001), as did non-Hispanic Black patients compared with non-Hispanic White patients (OR, 1.35; P =.0002). Participation was higher with cord blood grafts, mismatched unrelated donors, and certain diagnoses (eg, sickle cell disease). Lower participation was observed for severe aplastic anemia and haploidentical or peripheral blood grafts. Trial participation was not associated with OS in either group. Conclusions: Clinical trial participation remains low, particularly among autologous HSCT recipients, younger adults, and patients with specific diagnoses. Findings highlight the need to broaden trial eligibility, enhance outreach, and ensure equity in trial access to promote generalizable, patient-centered evidence in HSCT.
